name: Swiss Re AG
reason: Global reinsurer whose adjusted EPS went from USD 12.57 (2015) to 15.67 (2025), only 2.2%/yr, with a 2020 loss and USD 1-2.5 years in 2017-22 from nat-cat and reserve charges, 7.9% avg ROE and LTG ~1.8%; earnings set by catastrophe/reserving cycles (SCOR precedent).

name: UBS Group AG
reason: Leading global wealth franchise but earnings track market levels and investment-banking activity (adjusted EPS USD 1.47 to 2.75, -85% in 2023), ROIC 2.7%, a 16% adjusted-vs-GAAP gap, the ongoing Credit Suisse integration and the proposed Swiss extra-CET1 regime make 5-10y EPS unforecastable (RJF/AMP precedent).

name: Sparebank 1 Ostlandet
reason: Norwegian savings bank with 10.1% avg ROE, NOK EPS 17.91 near its rate-cycle peak (0.95x), share count +5.4%/yr from mergers and consensus -6.2%/+3.4%/+2.2% for FY1-FY3; fails the US through-cycle bank standard.

name: Acerinox SA
reason: Stainless-steel producer whose earnings follow nickel and steel prices: EUR EPS swung from 2.14 (2022) to -0.10 (2025), EBIT margin 2.6% (9th pctile) vs 12.4% peak, and net debt/EBITDA is 3.5x.

name: Unipol Assicurazioni SpA
reason: Italian motor-led multiline insurer whose EUR EPS rise (0.40 to 1.94) came with the UnipolSai merger and equity-accounted BPER/Pop Sondrio stakes at peak bank earnings, while revenue shrank 2.6%/yr, avg ROE is 9.9% and FY2 consensus is +2.9%; cheap-but-ordinary.

name: Unicaja Banco S.A.
reason: Spanish regional bank with 6.9% avg ROE and share count +10.3%/yr (Liberbank merger); EUR EPS of 0.24 (2025) is a rate-cycle high after 0.05 in 2020-21, so it fails the through-cycle bank standard.

name: Elkem ASA
reason: Silicon/silicones producer driven by commodity silicon prices: NOK EPS swung from 12.04 (2022) to -1.05 (2025), EBIT margin 1.3-20.8% and net debt/EBITDA 4.4x.

name: British American Tobacco p.l.c.
reason: Structurally declining cigarette volumes: GBP adjusted EPS grew only 1.2%/yr over 5y (3.32 in 2020 to 3.52 in 2025), the 51% adjusted-vs-GAAP gap reflects the US brand write-down, and consensus 2.6-8.2% leans on pricing and buybacks; NGP and regulation threaten the base (IMB precedent).

name: Optima Bank SA
reason: Fast-growing Greek challenger bank with 22% avg ROE and GAAP EPS EUR 0.45 (2021) to 0.77 (2025), but the public record is short (listed 2023), untested in a Greek credit downturn and earned during the rate cycle, so consensus +17-28% cannot be underwritten.

name: Atrium Ljungberg AB
reason: Stockholm property owner with FFO/share SEK 1.35 (2015) to 2.07 (2025), 4.3%/yr, net debt/EBITDA 12.8x and FY1 consensus -9.5%; rate-sensitive, leveraged and no 7% route.

name: Titan America SA
reason: US East Coast cement/aggregates with USD EPS 0.34 (2021) to 1.01 (2025) and EBIT margin at its 100th pctile (16.3% vs 12.3% avg) after a pricing upcycle (CRH/EXP near-peak precedent); only 5 years of data and ~87% Titan S.A. control.

name: Credito Emiliano SpA
reason: Well-run Italian bank but EUR EPS was flat at 0.59 through 2018-20 and jumped to 1.66-1.80 on rates; avg ROE 9.9%, consensus +2.5-5.9% and LTG 1.3% fail the US through-cycle bank standard (ISP precedent).

name: Hannover Rueck SE
reason: Low-cost, best-in-class reinsurer (EUR EPS 9.54 to 21.90, 8.7% 10y CAGR, 14.6% avg ROE) but EPS was flat through 2015-21 and is at a hard-market peak with consensus FY2/FY3 only +2.0%/+4.6%; P&C pricing and cat losses make 5-10y EPS unforecastable (KNSL/WRB precedent).

name: CTP N.V.
reason: Founder-controlled CEE logistics developer whose FFO growth (EUR 0.72 to 0.84 over 2023-25) is funded by development capex and debt (net debt/EBITDA 12.6x, acquisitions 1.07x FCF, GAAP EPS 69% above adjusted on revaluations); growth from leverage fails the test.

name: New Wave Group AB
reason: Promotional/sportswear group whose SEK EPS boomed to 8.81 (2022) and fell to 5.90 (0.67x peak) as EBIT margin went 7% to 16% to 12%; 9.4% avg ROIC, FCF conversion 0.61 and net debt 2.0x make it cheap-but-ordinary despite founder ownership.

name: GR. SARANTIS S.A.
reason: CEE mass-market cosmetics/household brands with EUR EPS 0.28 to 0.71 and net cash, but EBIT margin 10.9% is at its 10y high vs 8.3% avg, EPS fell 33% in 2022 on input costs, ROIC is 11.6% and growth relies on brand bolt-ons against P&G/Unilever and private label; cheap-but-ordinary.

name: Skandinaviska Enskilda Banken AB
reason: Wallenberg-anchored Nordic corporate bank that did grow through negative rates (SEK EPS 7.44 in 2017 to 11.67 in 2021, 13.2% avg ROE), but EPS (15.43) is down from an 18.06 rate peak, LTG is 2.5%, and its large-corporate/markets division ties earnings to capital-markets activity and Swedish CRE credit.

name: Centrica plc
reason: UK energy supplier/trader/producer whose GBP EPS is set by wholesale gas and power prices (0.04 in 2021 to 0.35 in 2022 to 0.11 in 2025), EBIT margin 1.9-49.7% and a 10y EPS CAGR of -4.5%.

name: K+S AG
reason: Potash and salt miner driven by potash prices: EUR EPS ranged from -9.42 (2020) to 16.13 (2021) to 0.70 (2025), 10y CAGR -12.9%, avg ROE 2.1%.

name: VusionGroup S.A.
reason: Global electronic-shelf-label leader in a secular retail-digitisation trend, but EUR EPS only turned durably positive in 2022 (6.04 in 2025), EBIT margin 7.4% is its 10y high, ROIC averages 3.4% and the Walmart roll-out concentration (single-customer) makes 5-10y earnings hard to forecast.
